title: Acceptance Criterion
description: A binary INSTRUCTION checking whether a feature does its job. Structured as three columns rather than prose so observability can be checked by machine. 'Never evaluated' is the ABSENCE of an ac_evaluation row, not a third verdict. Source: supabase/migrations/004_story_and_acceptance_criterion.sql

key.description: Globally unique (not per product). The pattern IS a database CHECK: key::text ~ '^ac_[a-z0-9]{6}$'. Stored as citext, so uniqueness is case-insensitive, but the CHECK itself is case-sensitive — uppercase is rejected.

when_.description: Trigger. Named with a trailing underscore because 'when' is a reserved word in SQL; the underscore is part of the wire name too.

then_.description: Observable outcome. Trailing underscore for the same reason as when_.

$comment: PARENTAGE NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: a criterion attaches to exactly one feature via feature_has_ac, which carries UNIQUE (criterion_id). Verdicts live in ac_evaluation (ac_verdict is pass|fail only), surfaced through latest_ac_state and feature_verified_state.
